title: Lehmer's totient problem with fewer than sixteen prime factors
journal_fit: The finite reductions, reproducible computational number theory, independently checked searches and primality certificates make a computational-number-theory journal the clearest fit.
contribution: The research revision establishes the stated sixteen-prime-factor lower bound and companion-equation results through written finite reductions and computations. It adds a one-candidate reduction for each prime prefix and independently checked primality certificates. Lehmer's full totient conjecture remains open.

abstract_tex: For a composite number $n$ whose totient divides $n-1$, earlier published work required fourteen prime factors, and computational announcements required fifteen. We prove a lower bound of sixteen, at least $16001$ if $(n-1)/\varphi(n)\ge3$, and more than $10^8$ if $3\mid n$, and that $n<2^{2^{k-7}}$ if $n$ has $k$ prime factors. For the companion equation $\varphi(n)\mid n+1$ we show that the nine known solutions are the only ones with at most eight prime factors, and that a further solution prime to $3$ has at least sixteen. Each statement is reduced by hand to a finite computation, which independent programs carry out. We also give a reduction with one candidate for the largest prime for each prefix. Lehmer's full conjecture remains open.
abstract_plain: For a composite number n whose totient divides n-1, earlier published work required fourteen prime factors, and computational announcements required fifteen. We prove a lower bound of sixteen, at least 16001 if (n-1)/phi(n)>=3, and more than 10^8 if 3 divides n, and that n<2^2^k-7 if n has k prime factors. For the companion equation phi(n) divides n+1 we show that the nine known solutions are the only ones with at most eight prime factors, and that a further solution prime to 3 has at least sixteen. Each statement is reduced by hand to a finite computation, which independent programs carry out. We also give a reduction with one candidate for the largest prime for each prefix. Lehmer's full conjecture remains open.
